function: Actor-critic DRL jointly selects each SMD's radio-map distribution mode, UAV-server computation allocation, and downlink bandwidth allocation of the UAV-to-SMD link to minimize delay-energy cost (p. 6).
system: UAV base station with MEC server serving 5-25 ground SMDs over a LoS downlink; antennas and carrier frequency not stated; 5-20 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (p. 3, p. 8).
method: Deterministic actor-critic deep reinforcement learning with replay buffer, target networks, and weighted actor loss for hybrid discrete-continuous actions; supervised sub-pixel CNN for radio-map super-resolution (p. 5, p. 7).
data_channel: Custom simulation: LoS free-space path loss h_i = beta0 d_i^-2, UAV-SMD distances 100-10000 m; no channel dataset or measurements (p. 3, p. 8).
test_conditions: Training setup not reported; evaluation over 5000 Monte Carlo trials varying SMDs (5-25), bandwidth (5-20 MHz), UAV-server (3-10 GHz) and SMD (0.5-3 GHz) capacities (p. 8, p. 9).
baselines: Non-learned: fixed modes All DEC, All DLC, All DCC, All ICC, and All Random; learned: DQN-based distribution-mode selection (p. 7, p. 8).
metrics: Average latency, average energy consumption, and average weighted cost per SMD of radio-map construction and distribution (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 3: "following the free-space path loss model" (h_i = beta0 d_i^-2). The channel is a custom LoS simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 8: "Fig. 5 further highlights the efficacy of our proposed scheme across varying numbers of SMDs". Settings are swept, but the paper never states that a policy trained in one setting is tested in another; the action vectors are sized by the number of SMDs (p. 6).
q3_support: p. 8: "34.97% lower average latency when compared to the DQN-based scheme" (learned baseline) and p. 8: "78.82% reduction compared to the ALL DEC scheme" (non-learned fixed mode; All Random also compared).
q4_support: p. 2: "This innovative approach effectively reduces the required training parameters". Only qualitative; no order of complexity, operation or parameter count, or runtime of the DRL is reported (the 186 ms on p. 8 is the system latency).
q5_support: p. 7: "The simulations are conducted within a UAV-assisted MEC network, as illustrated in Fig. 1." Custom simulation only; no code or data link and no public channel dataset.
notes: Title and DOI 10.1109/JIOT.2024.3378217 are on p. 1, so the PDF is the paper of the DOI. Borderline eligibility for the reviewer: the DRL action is (m, F, W) (p. 6), i.e., distribution/offloading mode and MEC computation allocation (above the physical layer) jointly with the bandwidth allocation W_i of the UAV-to-ground downlink (p. 3, Eq. 3). Under the aerial-link rule, learned resource allocation of an aerial link is physical layer and a joint decision passes the above_phy check, so I included it as area 6; the UAV transmit power is fixed at 500 mW (Table III, p. 8), so bandwidth is the only radio resource learned. The paper itself frames the algorithm as "joint computation offloading and resource allocation" (p. 2). The super-resolution CNN is adopted from [30] and shown only as image examples (Fig. 3, p. 6); its stated training speedup (p. 5) is a relative claim for that layer, not a cost of the proposed DRL, so q4 stays 0. No DRL hyperparameters or training episodes are reported.
